connectors.evidence_source: The metadata docs host redirects to Perigon's current provider-owned perigon.io documentation. Its .well-known/api-catalog declares api.perigon.io/v1 as the API item and links this service description. The downloaded artifact defines bearer apiKeyAuth; Perigon's current documentation also describes a free API plan and API-key enrollment.
connectors.counting_note: Perigon's current provider API catalog links this complete public OpenAPI artifact. It contains 33 paths and 45 HTTP operations: 26 GET, 11 POST, 4 PATCH, and 4 DELETE. GET actions are reads. Four POST actions are explicitly retrieval/search work and are semantic reads: cached article-refresh peek, Search Summarizer, vector news search, and vector Wikipedia search. The article-refresh job submission creates/schedules background processing, and the other POST actions create, activate, or pause contact points, monitors, source groups, and watchlists; together with all PATCH and DELETE actions, these are writes. Callable management of monitor/contact-point/source-group/watchlist objects is retained; no inbound delivery event is counted.

connectors.evidence_source: Pingdom's live provider-owned API reference labels the surface `Pingdom Public API (3.1)`, presents a Download link to this OpenAPI document, and its navigation covers Uptime, Alerting Settings, and Transaction API sections. Its authentication documentation says a Pingdom API token is generated in My Pingdom and is normally supplied through HTTP Bearer authentication, with Basic-token compatibility retained. The OpenAPI document identifies server `https://api.pingdom.com/api/3.1` and API version 3.1.
connectors.counting_note: Pingdom's rendered current API 3.1 reference directly links this complete provider-hosted OpenAPI artifact. Its 50 HTTP operation objects are 29 GET, five POST, seven PUT, and nine DELETE. Every GET retrieves actions, alerting contacts/teams, analysis, checks, credits, maintenance data, probes, reference data, results, summaries, transaction-check reports/checks, or traceroutes and is a read. The five POST operations expressly create contacts, teams, uptime checks, maintenance windows, or transaction checks; all PUT and DELETE operations expressly modify, pause, or delete provider state, so none is a semantic non-GET read. The artifact contains no API-token issuance or credential-management operation to exclude. Request/response schemas, rate-limit prose, examples, and UI concepts do not add callable actions.
